speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and whether they are itchy or painful? Also, has the child had any recent fevers or illnesses?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the daycare exposure and the recent chickenpox in the household, are the lesions fluid-filled vesicles that are appearing in crops at different stages of healing, or are they solid papules? I will also check for any associated fever or respiratory symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those pearly papules with central umbilication are classic for Molluscum Contagiosum, a common viral skin infection in young children. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum
